title: Group structure on the affinization of a flat separated trait group
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $G\to S$ be a flat, separated group scheme of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme here has multiplication $m:G\times_SG\to G$, identity $e:S\to G$ and inverse $i:G\to G$ satisfying the group diagrams; the product is the fibre product [def-pc-base-change]. Put $A=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$ and $H=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with the $S$-structure induced by $R\to A$. Let $u:G\to H$ be the canonical morphism corresponding to $\mathrm{id}_A$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Then $H$ has an $S$-group-scheme structure for which $u$ is a group homomorphism. More precisely, for the projections $p_1,p_2:G\times_SG\to G$, the natural homomorphism $A\otimes_R A\to\Gamma(G\times_SG,\mathcal O)$ sending $a\otimes b$ to $p_1^*a\,p_2^*b$ is an isomorphism, and multiplication, identity and inverse on $H$ are induced by $m^*,e^*,i^*$ through this isomorphism. No finite generation of $A$ as an $R$-algebra and no affineness of $G$ are assumed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/qrg.pdf: Proposition 3.1, printed p.5, paragraph beginning with the ring of global sections: the spectrum has a natural group structure even before finite generation of its ring is known. The product-of-sections assertion spells out the flat-over-a-DVR construction underlying that paragraph.

proof.text: The hypotheses give that $G$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]. The module $\mathcal O_G$ is invertible (it is free of rank one on itself) [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with this module and the domain $R$: $A$ is torsion-free over $R$. A DVR is a PID by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $A$ flat over $R$. In particular $H\to S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. This uses no finite generation of $A$.

source.place: Tag 0AUW, lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat (1); torsion-freeness argument in more-morphisms.tex, Tag 0EX8, lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, general-case proof.

proof.text: Let $q=u\times_S\mathrm{id}_G:G\times_SG\to H\times_SG$. For every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the second copy of $G$, $B$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] gives $\Gamma(G\times_SU,\mathcal O)=A\otimes_RB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\Gamma(H\times_SU,\mathcal O)=A\otimes_RB$ as well. Under these two identifications $q^*$ fixes $a\otimes b$: its value is the product of the pullbacks of $a$ and $b$, since $u^*$ is $\mathrm{id}_A$ by the definition of $u$. These are the actual pullback maps, so commute with restriction. The map between the two direct-image ring sheaves on $G$ is therefore an isomorphism on an affine basis, hence on all opens: local inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness, and glue by the sheaf axiom. Taking sections over $G$ proves that $q^*$ on global sections is an isomorphism. Finally apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] to $G$ and the flat affine base change $H\to S$ from step 1; it identifies $\Gamma(H\times_SG,\mathcal O)$ with $A\otimes_RA$. The composite is precisely $\beta_2:a\otimes b\mapsto p_1^*a\,p_2^*b$, proving the asserted isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, (2) with i=0; schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes. The basis-and-gluing assembly is written here.

proof.text: We also need injectivity in three factors to check associativity. The calculation of step 2 works with the second factor replaced by $G\times_SG$ or $H\times_SG$: both have affine open covers by products of affine opens, whose rings are $B\otimes_RC$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. The factors $B,C$ are flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. The tensor ring is flat: $B\to B\otimes_RC$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change], and its composite with the flat map $R\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. These product charts cover the second factor, so its stalks are flat and the factor is flat over $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], every affine open of that factor has flat section ring. Thus on its entire affine basis the same application of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] identifies pullback under replacement of the first $G$ by $H$ with $\mathrm{id}_{A\otimes_R(B\otimes_RC)}$; the local inverses glue as in step 2. Replace the first two factors successively in $G^3$, allowing a permutation of factors. Each replacement induces an isomorphism on global sections. For the resulting $H^2\times_SG$, apply flat base change to $G$ with affine base $H^2=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RA)$, whose ring is flat by the same argument. Consequently pullback by $u^3:G^3\to H^3$ is the isomorphism $\beta_3:A^{\otimes_R3}\to\Gamma(G^3,\mathcal O)$ sending $a\otimes b\otimes c$ to the product of their three pullbacks. In particular it is injective. All powers here mean fibre powers over $S$.

source.place: Tag 02KH, lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology (2); algebra.tex Tags 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change) and 00HC (lemma-composition-flat); schemes.tex Tag 01I4.

proof.text: Set $\Delta=\beta_2^{-1}\circ m^*:A\to A\otimes_RA$, $\epsilon=e^*:A\to R$, and $\sigma=i^*:A\to A$. They are $R$-algebra homomorphisms, because $m,e,i$ are $S$-morphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $H\times_SH=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RA)$. Take $m_H=\operatorname{Spec}\Delta$, $e_H=\operatorname{Spec}\epsilon$, and $i_H=\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$, using the contravariant spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. They are $S$-morphisms since their ring maps preserve $R$. Their definitions give $m_H\circ(u\times u)=u\circ m$, $e_H=u\circ e$, and $i_H\circ u=u\circ i$: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] these equalities can be checked on sections, where they say respectively $\beta_2\Delta=m^*$, $\epsilon=e^*$, and $\sigma=i^*$.

source.place: Tags 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine) and 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); explicit construction of the group operations in Prasad–Yu Proposition 3.1, p.5.

proof.text: Check the group diagrams, rather than assuming them from the construction. For maps $v,w:H^n\to H$, equality after precomposition by $u^n$ implies $v=w$: the affine-target correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] turns this into $\beta_n v^*=\beta_n w^*$, and $\beta_n$ is injective for $n=1,2,3$ (respectively $\mathrm{id}_A$, step 2 and step 3). Precompose the two associative products on $H^3$ by $u^3$. By step 4 the composites become $u\circ m\circ(m\times\mathrm{id})$ and $u\circ m\circ(\mathrm{id}\times m)$, equal by associativity on $G$. The two unit diagrams on $H$, precomposed by $u$, become $u\circ m\circ(e,\mathrm{id})=u$ and $u\circ m\circ(\mathrm{id},e)=u$. The two inverse diagrams, precomposed by $u$, become $u\circ m\circ(i,\mathrm{id})=u\circ e\circ(G\to S)$ and the corresponding equality with the factors reversed. These are precisely the identity and inverse axioms on $G$. The injectivity just proved descends all these equalities to $H$. Thus $H$ is an $S$-group scheme; step 4 makes $u$ a homomorphism and gives exactly the three specified pullbacks. No assertion that $u$ is surjective, that $G$ is affine, or that $A$ is finitely generated was used.

The relations follow because (u×u)^♯=β2, and the group axioms pass down to H because maps into an affine target are determined by global sections and β1, β2, β3 are injective. Both steps are correctly marked elementary. Small cases I tested: G_a, G_m, μ_p in residue characteristic p, a proper elliptic curve (A=R, u not injective) and a disconnected special fibre. lean.note: The canonical tensor comparison is stated equivalently as the pushout square of commutative rings over R with legs the actual projection pullbacks. The group structure is on Spec Γ(G) with the induced R-structure; the over-arrow is required to have underlying map G.toSpecΓ. IsMonHom gives multiplication and unit compatibility, and GrpObj.inv_hom gives inverse compatibility, hence the three specified induced operations.
